# **Problem Description** 

Students often lack practical programming and software development experience, resulting in difficulties with project structure, self-estimation, acceptance criteria, testing, and Agile practices. Many students rely on AI or learn by doing, but the quality and consistency of their work can vary, and they may struggle to understand the overall project progress. In addition, students tend to form groups based on skill levels, which can create uneven team performance. From the instructor’s perspective, existing tools such as Excel, Google Sheets, Notion, Trello, and Jira either lack standardized formats, provide limited project management features, are difficult to use, or have access limitations. Therefore, a standardized and accessible project management tool with structured templates, task tracking, Agile support, progress reporting, and feedback mechanisms could help students better understand project practices and improve their work based on instructor feedback.

# **Target Customers**

- **Auditor** ( Person who can inspect projects eg. TAs and Professors ) : Able to review, comment and edit any project  
- **Team members** ( Students ) : Create & Manage projects, Assign tickets to other team members

# **Functional Requirements**

### **User Access & Role Management System**

* The system shall allow users to authenticate before accessing the platform.  
* The system shall support **Team Member** and **Auditor** roles.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to manage projects in which they participate.  
* The system shall allow Auditors to inspect, review, comment on, and edit projects according to Auditor permissions.  
* The system shall prevent users from performing actions outside their authorized permissions.

### **Project Management System**

* The system shall allow Team Members to create and manage projects.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to define a project name and description.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to configure a project as **General Mode** or **SE Mode**.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to create projects using predefined project templates.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to add other Team Members to a project.  
* The system shall enable SE-specific capabilities when SE Mode is selected.

### **Ticket & Backlog Management System**

* The system shall allow Team Members to create and manage Tickets in a project.  
* The system shall support **User Story, Task, and Bug** Ticket types in SE Mode.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to define Acceptance Criteria for User Stories.  
* The system shall provide User Story structure guidance in SE Mode.  
* The system shall provide Story Point estimation guidance in SE Mode.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to assign Story Points to Tickets.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to prioritize Tickets in the Backlog.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to assign or reassign Tickets to other Team Members in the same project.

### **Sprint Management System**

* The system shall allow Team Members to create and manage Sprints.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to define Sprint start and end dates.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to assign Tickets from the Backlog to a Sprint.  
* The system shall calculate planned Story Points for a Sprint when estimation data is available.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to update Ticket workflow status during a Sprint.  
* The system shall support workflow states such as **To Do, In Progress, Review, and Done**.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to mark Tickets as **Blocked** and provide a reason.  
* The system shall record Ticket status changes during Sprint execution.  
* The system shall calculate Sprint progress and Burndown information.  
* The system shall allow unfinished Tickets to return to the Backlog or move to another Sprint.

### **Auditor Review & Feedback System**

* The system shall allow Auditors to inspect any project according to Auditor permissions.  
* The system shall allow Auditors to inspect project Backlogs, Sprints, and Tickets.  
* The system shall allow Auditors to view Sprint progress and Burndown information.  
* The system shall allow Auditors to provide review comments and feedback on projects.  
* The system shall allow Auditors to provide comments on specific Tickets where applicable.  
* The system shall record the Auditor identity and timestamp for each review or comment.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to view feedback provided by Auditors.  
* The system shall maintain review and feedback history.

### **Sprint Review & Reporting System**

* The system shall allow Team Members to generate a **Sprint Review Summary**.  
* The system shall summarize Planned Work and Completed Work for the selected Sprint.  
* The system shall identify Carry-over and Blocked Tickets where applicable.  
* The system shall generate the Sprint Review Summary from recorded Sprint and Ticket data.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to review the generated summary before use.  
* The system shall allow Team Members to select available Sprint metrics for inclusion in the summary.  
* The system shall allow the Sprint Review Summary to be exported or used for presentation.  
* The system shall identify missing information when a complete Sprint Summary cannot be generated.

# **Non-functional Requirements**

### **Operational**

* The system shall provide a web-based interface accessible through commonly used modern browsers.  
* The system shall support both desktop and mobile screen sizes.  
* The system shall preserve Project, Ticket, Sprint, and Review data between user sessions.  
* The system shall provide backup and recovery mechanisms for project-management data.  
* The system shall provide consistent terminology and navigation across Project, Backlog, Sprint, Ticket, and Auditor interfaces.

### **Performance**

* The system shall provide responsive interactions for common Project, Backlog, Ticket, and Sprint operations.  
* The system shall display Project Boards and Auditor Dashboards without noticeable delay during normal usage.  
* The system shall calculate Sprint progress and Burndown information without significantly interrupting normal Ticket operations.  
* The system shall generate Sprint Review Summaries within an acceptable interactive response time.  
* The system shall avoid unnecessary recalculation of project metrics when the underlying project data has not changed.

### **Security**

* The system shall require users to authenticate before accessing protected functions.  
* The system shall enforce authorization based on **Team Member** and **Auditor** roles.  
* The system shall restrict Team Members from accessing or modifying unrelated projects unless explicitly authorized.  
* The system shall allow Auditor capabilities only to authenticated users with Auditor permissions.  
* The system shall enforce authorization on the server side and shall not rely only on user-interface restrictions.  
* The system shall protect project, user, review, and authentication data from unauthorized access.

### **Scalability**

* The system shall support an increasing number of Projects without requiring major changes to the core architecture.  
* The system shall support an increasing number of Team Members and Auditors.  
* The system shall support growth in the number of Tickets, Sprints, and Review records within each Project.  
* The system architecture shall allow SE-specific features or plugins to be added without redesigning the Core Project Management functionality.  
* The system shall allow individual business capabilities to be separated or scaled independently in future versions if required.

### **Data Integrity**

* The system shall prevent Project, Ticket, Sprint, and Review data from being stored in an invalid or incomplete state.  
* The system shall maintain valid relationships between Projects, Team Members, Tickets, and Sprints.  
* The system shall prevent Tickets from being assigned to users who are not Team Members of the corresponding Project.  
* The system shall preserve Ticket status history and Sprint history after updates are made.  
* The system shall derive Sprint Progress, Burndown, and Sprint Review Summary information from recorded Ticket and Sprint data.  
* The system shall ensure that updates to Ticket assignments, Story Points, workflow status, and Sprint membership are stored consistently.  
* The system shall preserve Auditor review and comment records together with the corresponding author and timestamp.

# **Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)**

**ADR-001: Frontend Framework**

| Title | Frontend Framework |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Context** | Chura requires a responsive web interface for Team Members and Auditors. The frontend must support project creation, ticket and backlog management, Sprint boards, progress visualization, Auditor review, and Sprint Review Summary workflows. The project is in an early pilot stage, so the team needs a framework that supports fast development, reusable UI components, maintainable routing, and future extension without introducing unnecessary infrastructure complexity. |
| **Decision** | Use Next.js with React as the frontend framework for Chura. |
| **Status** | **Accepted** |
| **Consequences** | **Positive** ·  	Provides a structured React framework with built-in routing and application conventions. ·  	Supports responsive web application development for both Team Member and Auditor workflows. ·  	Allows reuse of the React ecosystem for boards, forms, charts, and other project-management UI components. ·  	Supports future server-side rendering or server-side data fetching if the product later needs them. ·  	Keeps the frontend technology widely understandable for student developers. **Negative** ·  	Introduces Next.js-specific concepts that the development team must learn. ·  	The team must define clear boundaries between frontend state, API state, and backend business rules. ·  	Some Next.js capabilities may be unnecessary during the first pilot if the application behaves mainly as an authenticated dashboard. |

 

**ADR-002: Backend Framework**

| Title | Backend Framework |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Context** | Chura requires backend logic for authentication and authorization, project management, ticket assignment, backlog management, Sprint execution, progress metrics, Auditor review, and reporting. The backend should support the proposed Modular Monolith architecture with clear business-module boundaries. The development team needs a framework that is structured enough to prevent the codebase from becoming an unorganized monolith, while remaining simple to deploy during the pilot. The backend must also support server-side authorization because Auditor and Team Member permissions cannot rely only on frontend restrictions. |
| **Decision** | Use Go (Golang) as the backend language and framework foundation for Chura. |
| **Status** | **Accepted** |
| **Consequences** | **Positive** ·  	Provides static typing and compile-time checking for backend reliability. ·  	Produces a single deployable binary, simplifying deployment for the pilot. ·  	Provides strong concurrency support for handling multiple project, ticket, and dashboard requests. ·  	Has a small runtime footprint and good performance for API workloads. ·  	Supports clear package boundaries that can align with the Modular Monolith structure. **Negative** ·  	The development team must be familiar with Go conventions, interfaces, error handling, and package design. ·  	Go provides less framework-level structure out of the box than highly opinionated frameworks such as NestJS, so the team must define architectural conventions carefully. |

**ADR-003: CSS / UI Framework**

| Title | CSS / UI Framework |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Context** | Chura contains UI-heavy workflows such as Project setup, Backlog management, ticket forms, Sprint boards, dashboards, Auditor review, and report presentation. The interface must be responsive, consistent, and quick to implement by a student development team. Options considered include Tailwind CSS, Bootstrap, Ant Design, and component libraries built on top of React. Bootstrap provides predefined styles but can make customization less flexible. Ant Design offers many ready-made enterprise components but introduces a stronger visual system and component dependency than the project currently needs. The project benefits from a styling approach that works naturally with Next.js, supports responsive design, and allows the team to build a custom visual identity without maintaining large custom CSS files. |
| **Decision** | Use Tailwind CSS as the primary CSS/UI framework for Chura. Use Tailwind utility classes for layout, spacing, typography, responsive behavior, and reusable visual patterns. Shared UI patterns such as buttons, forms, cards, tickets, and board columns should be implemented as reusable React components so that utility classes are not duplicated inconsistently across pages. |
| **Status** | **Proposed** |
| **Consequences** | **Positive** •	Supports rapid UI development and responsive design. •	Integrates well with Next.js and React component workflows. •	Allows fine-grained customization without being locked into a predefined visual theme. •	Reduces the need for large global CSS files. •	Makes it easier to create consistent spacing, sizing, and responsive behavior across Project, Sprint, and Auditor views. **Negative** •	Utility-heavy markup can become difficult to read if component boundaries are poor. •	The team must define reusable component patterns to avoid inconsistent class combinations. •	Tailwind does not provide complete enterprise widgets by itself, so complex components such as data grids or advanced charts may still require additional libraries. |
